brief.headline: Aluminium broke away from the rest of the metals complex: the 29-Jul official jumped 1.07% to $3,177 on Gulf escalation and a near-7% surge in oil while copper actually FELL 0.4% - and the cash-3M backwardation almost doubled to +$30.00 as stock drew to 267,800 t, a fresh century low.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the 29-Jul official rose across the board - cash $3,207.00 (+$47.50, +1.50%) and 3M $3,177.00 (+$33.50, +1.07%) - recovering all of Tuesday's fall and closing at the strongest official cash since 22-Jul. Warehouse stock drew another 1,500 t to 267,800 t, and freely available (on-warrant) metal is down to 245,350 t, a 16-month low.

WHY: this was a metal story, not a macro one - the exact reverse of Tuesday. Oil jumped nearly 7% on escalating Middle East airstrikes and Iran's rejection of Oman's Hormuz proposal, reviving supply fear around the roughly 9% of global capacity sitting behind that waterway. Crucially the dollar was NEAR ONE-MONTH HIGHS and copper fell 0.4% on the same session: aluminium rose in spite of the macro, alone in the complex.

THE SIGNAL THAT MATTERS: price UP and backwardation WIDER - +$30.00 from +$16.00, nearly double in one session - is the aligned tightening configuration, and it followed Tuesday's price-down/spread-wider squeeze signature. Two consecutive sessions of a widening prompt premium, through both a selloff and a rally, is a more durable tightness signal than either day alone. The 29-Jul cash also edged above the 22-Jul high at $3,205, a marginal but real upside break.

WATCH THIS WEEK: the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% but with THREE dissents for a HIKE and the 30-year yield at its highest since 2007 - the tightening risk did not go away, it was deferred. Next: the Bank of England at noon London today (3.75%, hold ~86% priced), China's July PMI tomorrow 31-Jul (June 50.3), whether stock breaks 265,000 t, and whether Hormuz transits keep resuming after the first LNG tanker exited in nearly three weeks.

drivers.text: EU CBAM's definitive phase plus the 4%-to-6% duty reversion are both embedded in the European premium, with TTF gas capping any restart — CBAM entered its definitive phase on 01-Jan-2026, so importers of primary aluminium into the EU now surrender certificates against embedded emissions rather than merely reporting them, and the EU import duty reverted from 4% to 6% on 01-Jan-2026. No alumina-refinery-grade lime assessment is published publicly and there is no liquid global index - the causticisation reagent is largely regional and contract-priced, so this generic average is indicative only.

notes: Alumina remains the comfortable part of the cost stack. Ex-China marks sit in a $309-330/t band - SMM $328/t FOB Western Australia (09-Jul), Platts FOB Australia $330/t (26-Jun) and the CME Platts-linked future at $309.40/t (24-Jul) - against an LME 3M of $3,177 on the 29-Jul official. On a 2:1 alumina-to-aluminium input ratio that is roughly 20.6% of the metal price, close to the ~19% level the industry treats as normal and far from the >30% squeeze territory of 2024-25.

The direction of travel is still surplus. S&P Global CERA models a 1.79 Mt global alumina SURPLUS for 2026, narrowing from 2.4 Mt in 2025, and EGA's Al Taweelah refinery has been restarting since 10-Jul after a three-and-a-half-month outage with full capability targeted by end-2026. Rio Tinto's H1-2026 alumina output was 4,040 kt, +8% y/y.

NEW OFFSET THIS RUN: Rio Tinto disclosed on 29-Jul that Yarwun will be CUT 40% from October 2026 on tailings-storage constraints. That is a genuine Q4 subtraction from the Australian surplus and the first material supply-side offset to the ex-China glut narrative in several weeks. It does not reverse the surplus, but it does argue against extrapolating the July softening.

China's domestic market stays soft and range-bound: the SMM Alumina Index was CNY 2,730.17/mt on 16-Jul, -12.8 w/w, with Mysteel's national weighted average CNY 2,762/t on 10-Jul and near-term guidance of CNY 2,600-2,750/t. The operating rate was 75.04% on 88.86 Mt/y of operating capacity. Import parity remains shut, so the two markets are not arbitraging.

STALENESS DISCLOSURE: every alumina and raw-material line in this report is a PERIODIC assessment carried at its own labelled date, not a 30-Jul value. The freshest are SMM 09-Jul (FOB WA), CME 24-Jul (futures) and SMM 16-Jul (China index). Bauxite is materially staler - the freshest publicly retrievable Guinea CIF China print is early June - because SMM's live assessments are paywalled.

The feedstock IS dated and rising: Shandong green petcoke settled the June cycle at CNY 3,727.4/t for 3A (+30.5 MoM), 3,470.5 for 3B and 2,868.8 for 3C (published 17-Jul), which is pushing calcined costs up. items.label: Coal tar pitch (CTP)
items.note: Modified CTP June settlement cycle: Shandong CNY 4,938/t (+96 MoM) and Shanxi CNY 4,940/t (+214 MoM), published 17-18 Jul-2026; H1-2026 average CNY 5,009.2/t. Anode binder and a by-product of steel coke ovens, so supply is tied to steel output and the spot market is thin. CTP is 14.95% of prebaked anode cost.

items.label: Pre-baked anodes
items.note: CNY 5,683/t cash (5,707 acceptance) - July 2026 procurement benchmark at a major Shandong smelter, +CNY 30/t month-on-month, published 17-18 Jul-2026. This SNAPPED a run of declines. Production cost is about CNY 5,615.92/t so the average producer margin is only +CNY 67.08/t - margins hover just above breakeven. H2-2026 expected range CNY 5,100-5,800/t on ample supply and firm demand.

items.label: Electricity (smelter power)
items.note: NO DATED 2026 PUBLIC BENCHMARK EXISTS - power is contracted bilaterally and not publicly assessed, so this range is indicative only. Secondary references put China smelters at roughly $40-60/MWh, Europe $70-110/MWh and Canada $26.50-41.00/MWh, with long-term contract economics around $40/MWh against a global specific consumption of ~13,990 kWh/t. The dated, tradeable proxies moved AGAINST smelters this run: Brent +3.64% to $87.15 on 29-Jul and TTF at EUR 56.37/MWh, +31.65% month-on-month with EU storage 54.2% full against 65% a year earlier. Europe's $1,200-1,500/t energy cost versus $650-850/t elsewhere remains the structural swing factor.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: The picture turned two-way for the first time in weeks. On 29-Jul Tehran REJECTED Oman's proposed 50-50 arrangement for managing the strait and airstrikes widened, sending crude up nearly 7% to roughly $90.5/bbl Brent - and Reuters attributed aluminium's 0.9% intraday gain directly to the resulting Gulf supply worry, on a session when copper fell 0.4%. THEN ON 30-JUL a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited Hormuz bound for Pakistan, the FIRST in nearly three weeks, and oil slipped as tankers continued to ply conflict-zone waters. Roughly 9% of global primary aluminium capacity and about 80-85% of Gulf aluminium exports depend on this route; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June at 332 kt following the March smelter attacks. Commercial transits were at a three-week low as of 27-Jul against…

logistics.label: Red Sea corridor
logistics.note: Bab el-Mandeb traffic has been reported steady despite the Houthi threat, keeping the Suez routing viable for Europe-bound metal and alumina. This remains the less binding of the two chokepoints, but it is a second-order exposure that would compound sharply if Hormuz stays shut into Q4.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk premiums for Gulf transits are quoted at 3-10% of hull value against roughly 0.25% before the conflict - $3m-$10m on a $100m vessel versus about $250,000 - after Iran resumed tanker attacks and struck two UAE supertankers on 14-Jul. Roughly $7m per transit is the commonly cited working figure. Around 6,000 seafarers were reported trapped in the region. This is the single largest non-tariff cost wedge in Gulf-origin delivered prices and it re-escalated with the 29-Jul news.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: Off a mid-month peak near 2,944. Dry-bulk direction matters most for bauxite and alumina freight into China, where Guinea shipped a record 114.8 Mt in H1. Easing bulk rates partly offset the war-risk wedge on the alumina leg.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: Drewry's World Container Index fell 4% to $4,374 per 40ft on 23-Jul, with Shanghai-Rotterdam at $4,824, after peaking at $4,639 on 09-Jul - the highest since September 2024 and roughly 61% above a year earlier. Direction is easing, but several carriers have filed Emergency Fuel Surcharges effective August 2026 on continued Hormuz disruption, so realised container cost falls more slowly than the index.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, remained in force as of 20-Jul. Contract mechanics - war-risk clauses, demurrage exposure and force-majeure triggers - remain live commercial variables wherever Gulf-origin metal or Hormuz-transiting alumina is involved. Indonesia has separately delayed alumina and nickel shipments over a regulatory gap on rare-earth content in cargoes, with no rule defining a maximum allowable level.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: Brent is around $90.48 at this 30-Jul refresh, easing 0.29% after a NEAR-7% SURGE on 29-Jul on escalating Middle East airstrikes and Tehran's rejection of Oman's Hormuz control proposal - up from roughly $87.15 the prior day. That surge is the direct proximate cause of aluminium's 29-Jul outperformance. The read-across is two-sided: energy is the single largest smelter cost line, so the same escalation that lifts the metal also lifts the cost of producing it. Oil slipped on 30-Jul as tankers continued to ply conflict-zone waters. (Trading Economics / Business Recorder)

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: DXY around 100.88, easing about 0.37% from the 101.26 carried on 29-Jul, with Trading Economics showing +0.06% on the current tick. THE KEY POINT FOR THIS RUN: Reuters described the dollar as NEAR ONE-MONTH HIGHS during the 29-Jul session, with roughly 30% priced on a 25bp Fed hike - and aluminium rose 1.07% anyway while copper fell 0.4%. A metal that appreciates into a firm dollar is being repriced on its own supply fundamentals, not on macro beta. That is the inverse of Tuesday, when a firm dollar sold the whole complex.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD around 1.14575, up roughly 0.48% from 1.14022 on 29-Jul. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.25% on 23-Jul. The euro-side energy exposure remains the residual constraint: TTF gas is around EUR 60.8/MWh, having touched EUR 64.02/MWh on 24-Jul, an 18-week high, with EU storage well behind last year - a live brake on any European smelter restart, and now compounded by the fresh Brent move.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: Yuan 6.76064, firming about 0.15%. China's operating primary capacity reached 45.31 Mt/y at end-June, BREACHING its own 45 Mt ceiling. Domestic ingot destocking continues but from a historically high seasonal base, and aluminium BILLET social inventory in major consumption regions rose to 121,000 t as at 23-Jul, a second consecutive weekly build - an off-season demand signal that cuts directly against the ex-China tightness story. SHFE registered cast aluminium alloy warrants were 17,341 t on 29-Jul, -148 t on the day.

row.label: USD/JPY
row.note: Yen 163.425, effectively unchanged. A weak yen cushions Japan-bound cargo premia in local terms. MJP Q4 talks open around late August against the decade-high $395/t Q3 anchor; no public producer offers have been reported yet. Japanese port stocks at 238,000 t end-May were the lowest since February 2012, -28.1% y/y - a genuinely tight physical backdrop for that negotiation, and the widening LME backwardation strengthens the producers' hand into it.

row.label: US 10Y yield
row.note: 10Y 4.686%, up about 7bp from 4.614% on 29-Jul. The more significant move was at the long end: the 30-YEAR YIELD REACHED ITS HIGHEST LEVEL SINCE 2007 after the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% with three dissents FOR a hike, as the bond market questioned whether the Committee is moving fast enough on inflation above target for more than five years. The Dow fell 1,153 points on the day. Higher long rates raise the carry cost of holding metal, which is itself a mechanical contributor to backwardation.

headlines.title: The Fed HELD at 3.50-3.75% but the composition matters more than the decision: a 9-3 vote with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting in favour of a 25bp HIKE - the most dissents opposite to the majority since September 2016, with inflation above target for more than five years. The Dow fell 1,153 points and the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007. Tightening risk has been deferred, not removed, and the next FOMC is 15-16 September with an SEP. The Bank of England follows at noon London today with Bank Rate at 3.75% and a hold ~86% priced.
headlines.source: CNBC - Fed rate decision July 2026 (29-Jul-2026); Business Recorder - Fed holds rates steady, three policymakers dissent in favor of a hike (29-Jul-2026)

headlines.title: Escalation drove the metal. Oil jumped nearly 7% on 29-Jul on widening Middle East airstrikes after Tehran REJECTED Oman's proposal for Hormuz control, taking Brent to roughly $90.5/bbl, and Reuters attributed aluminium's rise directly to worries about Gulf metal supply. Roughly 9% of global primary capacity sits behind that waterway and Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June. COUNTERPOINT, 30-Jul: a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited the strait bound for Pakistan, the first in nearly three weeks, and oil eased as tankers continued to ply conflict-zone waters - the first tentative sign transits may be normalising.
headlines.source: Business Recorder - Oil jumps nearly 7% on escalating Middle East airstrikes (29-Jul-2026); Tehran rejects Omani proposal for Hormuz control (29-Jul-2026); QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker heads to Pakistan after exiting Hormuz (30-Jul-2026)

headlines.title: Ex-Gulf supply keeps landing on a slower clock. Century Aluminum's Mt. Holly returned to FULL capacity on 27-Jul for the first time since 2015 after a $50m restart, adding roughly 10% to US primary output; EGA's Al Taweelah alumina refinery has been ramping since 10-Jul with full capability targeted by end-2026; Indonesia is adding around 705 kt this year; and China's operating primary capacity has BREACHED its own 45 Mt ceiling at 45.31 Mt/y. Rio Tinto's AP60 Arvida adds 160 kt/y by end-2026, though Yarwun alumina will be cut 40% from October on tailings constraints.
headlines.source: SC Daily Gazette / AL Circle - Century Mt. Holly at full capacity (27-Jul-2026); Rio Tinto H1-2026 results (29-Jul-2026)

headlines.title: The listed producer P&Ls are unanimous that the current price-and-premium regime is generating exceptional upstream margin even on flat volumes: Rio Tinto's aluminium EBITDA +31% in H1 on 1,676 kt of flat primary output (29-Jul), Norsk Hydro's Q2 adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m, +15% y/y and above consensus (22-Jul), and Alcoa's record Aluminum-segment EBITDA of $1.073bn at a 32.3% margin (16-Jul). Vedanta Aluminium Metal reports Q1 FY27 today after a record 632 kt production quarter; Century Aluminum follows on 6 August.
headlines.source: Rio Tinto H1-2026 (29-Jul-2026); Norsk Hydro Q2-2026 (22-Jul-2026); AL Circle - Vedanta Aluminium record Q1 FY27 output (Jul-2026)

headlines.title: China's July NBS manufacturing PMI lands tomorrow, 31-Jul, against 50.3 in June (May 50.0), a third consecutive month of expansion. Domestic aluminium ingot destocking continues but from a historically high base for the season, and SHFE registered cast aluminium alloy warrants stood at 17,341 t on 29-Jul, down 148 t on the day. Aluminium billet social inventory in major consumption regions rose to 121,000 t as at 23-Jul, a second consecutive week of build - an off-season demand signal that cuts against the ex-China tightness.
headlines.source: SMM / Shanghai Metals Market via AL Circle - China aluminium inventory and SHFE warrant data (late Jul-2026)

forward.basis: LME official prices via Westmetall. Baseline = LME 3-month official (a traded market price). Range = random-walk cone from realized volatility. Driver score = 3 transparent rules, hit rate measured on history.
forward.source: London Metal Exchange official settlements via Westmetall (https://www.westmetall.com/en/markdaten.php?action=table&field=LME_Al_cash)
forward.stance_label: Current physical-market condition (diagnostic, not a forecast)

drivers.name: Curve carry (cash − 3M)
drivers.rule: Backwardation (cash above 3M) = prompt physical tightness = bullish; contango = bearish.

drivers.name: Inventory trend (13-week)
drivers.rule: LME stock falling more than 2% over 13 weeks = tightening = bullish; rising >2% = bearish.

drivers.name: Momentum (3M vs 20-week average)
drivers.rule: Price above its 20-week average = uptrend = bullish; below = bearish.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 39.2% directional hit rate against a 72.5% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 2.09% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (97 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-05-01). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: Q2 2026 BEAT: adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y vs NOK 7,790m; above consensus); Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 6,421m; adjusted EPS NOK 2.2 (from NOK 1.7); free cash flow NOK 4bn; 12-month adjusted RoaCE 10.9%. Shares rose on the print. First European producer P&L of the Hormuz-disruption quarter. Higher aluminium prices and product premiums plus stronger recycling earnings drove the beat; a stronger NOK and lower hydro-power output were partial offsets. Confirms the disruption-quarter price/premium is translating into real producer margin - a positive read-across for the smelter complex.

June-quarter production report: Worsley alumina 943 kt, Hillside aluminium 179 kt; group beat FY26 production guidance with quarterly sales +15%. Sale of the aluminium value chain to Alcoa (announced 01-Jul) progressing. Beat group production guidance with aluminium 1% above plan; Hillside 717 kt, Mozal 248 kt and Brazil Aluminium 144 kt for FY26, quarterly sales volumes +15%. FY26 FINANCIAL results are scheduled for 27 August 2026. The Alcoa transaction - up to $5.6bn for the bauxite, alumina and aluminium value chain ($4.1bn upfront, Mozal excluded) - is expected to close in H1-2027 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.

Revenue $3.97bn (+24% q/q, highest in nearly a decade); adj. EPS $2.12 (MISS vs ~$2.31 consensus); adj. net income $562m; adj. EBITDA $901m (from $595m in Q1); Aluminum segment RECORD EBITDA $1.073bn at 32.3% margin. First producer P&L under the Hormuz-disruption regime: record aluminium margins and near-decade-high revenue on higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums, but adj. EPS missed on higher costs — notably ~$35m more Section-232 tariff on Canadian metal into the US — and the shares fell. South32 upstream acquisition ($4.1bn upfront, up to $5.6bn contingent to 2030) progressing, close expected H1-2027. The tariff is a double edge: it inflates US premia but taxes Alcoa's cross-border Canadian metal.

Group revenue $31.0bn (+15%); underlying EBITDA $14.8bn (+28%); free cash flow +75%; dividend raised. ALUMINIUM segment EBITDA +31%. Primary aluminium 1,676 kt (flat), alumina 4,040 kt (+8%), bauxite 28.5 Mt (-7%). Reported this morning and the freshest producer datapoint in this report. A 31% rise in aluminium EBITDA on flat volumes is a pure price-and-premium effect, confirming that the current regime is generating exceptional upstream margins. Two supply items matter for the forward view: Yarwun output will be CUT 40% from October 2026 (~1.2 Mt/y) on tailings constraints, extending life to 2035, and AP60 Arvida ($1.5bn, +160 kt/y) completes commissioning by end-2026.

Guides H1-26 net profit ¥1.8–1.95bn, +154.4–175.6% YoY. Credits industry-chain cost reduction, aluminium prices fluctuating at highs, high-value-added deep-processing mix and energy-saving retrofits — the first sizeable China H1 pre-announcement of the season and a positive read-across for Chinese producer margins.

Hindalco PAT ₹5,283cr (+66% YoY); India Al upstream EBITDA margin ~46%; Novelis FY26 adj. EBITDA $1.6bn (−9%). Record India operations; Novelis pressured by Oswego outage (~$104m) and tariffs (~$143m).

Net profit $200.3m (+316% YoY); EPS 53 fils; sales −17% on Gulf supply-chain disruption. LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.

Q1-2026 missed estimates with sales up year-on-year. Q2-2026 results confirmed for Thursday 6 August 2026 after market close, call 17:00 ET. The cleanest listed read on US Section-232 economics. Mt. Holly returned to FULL capacity on 27-Jul for the first time since 2015 after a $50m potline restart, adding roughly 10% to total US primary aluminium output and taking the workforce above 600; Century credited the tariff regime explicitly. The 6 August print will be the first to show what a $2,380/t Midwest duty-paid premium does to a US-domiciled smelter's P&L.

Net profit SAR 1.63bn, +6% year-on-year; gross profit -2% on higher cost of sales with lower phosphate and aluminium volumes. Listed-company public disclosure. Q2-2026 results date has not been announced publicly on Tadawul at this refresh. Included for peer comparability only, on the same public listed-company basis as the other producers in this table.
Net profit guided RMB 5.30–5.59bn (+50–58% YoY). Strong on higher Al prices; China output near self-imposed 45 Mt capacity cap.
FY25 net loss $455m (vs $803m profit in 2024) on higher costs & lower output. Analysts expect stronger H1 2026 on higher prices; Asia pivot amid fractured trade flows.
FY25 results; copper & aluminium average prices +9% YoY; zinc metal +4%. Resilient structural demand for Cu/Al cited; broadly constructive sector tone.
Underlying profit $6.2bn (+>20%); underlying EBITDA $15.5bn (+25%, 58% margin); interim div 73c. Copper-led strength; broad base-metals read-across positive for the complex.

catalysts.text: BANK OF ENGLAND MPC decision and full Monetary Policy Report, 12:00 London, with a Governor's press conference at 13:00. Bank Rate is 3.75% and a hold is roughly 86% priced on SONIA futures against ~14% for a rise to 4.00%; services inflation keeps the hike risk live. A second major central bank signalling persistent inflation risk reinforces the rates headwind the Fed left in place

Today's LME official (13:20 London) - the tell is whether the cash-3M backwardation HOLDS above +$25.00 now that the Fed event has passed, and whether the fresh break above the 22-Jul $3,205 pivot is confirmed by a second consecutive close above it

Vedanta Aluminium Metal Q1 FY27 results (board meeting plus a 17:00 IST earnings call) after a RECORD 632 kt production quarter, +5% y/y, with value-added output a record 389 kt, +14% y/y. The first look at what a record Indian volume quarter earns at current LME levels

China NBS July manufacturing and non-manufacturing PMI. June was 50.3 and 50.2 respectively, a third consecutive month of expansion; a sub-50 print would be the clearest demand-side negative available this week, and it lands against billet social inventory that has built for two consecutive weeks

HORMUZ TRANSIT COUNT IS NOW THE KEY VARIABLE: a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited the strait on 30-Jul, the first in nearly three weeks. Whether that becomes a trend or a one-off determines the largest single component of the current supply premium
LME stock trajectory - whether the uninterrupted July draw takes inventory through 265,000 t, and whether AVAILABLE on-warrant metal falls below the current 16-month low of 245,350 t
China Caixin manufacturing PMI - the private-survey cross-check on the NBS print, weighted toward smaller exporters and therefore more sensitive to the closed semis export arbitrage

Century Aluminum Q2-2026 results after market close, call 17:00 ET. The cleanest listed read on US Section-232 economics and the first print to show what a ~$2,380/t Midwest duty-paid premium does to a US-domiciled smelter's P&L, with Mt. Holly now back at full capacity

US July nonfarm payrolls. June added just 57,000 jobs with April and May revised down by a combined 74,000; another weak print would cut against the three hawkish FOMC dissents and unwind the dollar bid
US July CPI - the variable behind the three dissents, with inflation above the 2% target for more than five years. The most direct input to whether September brings a hike

MJP Q4-2026 premium negotiations open against the decade-high $395/t Q3 settlement, now with a two-session widening LME backwardation and a fresh century low in exchange stock behind the producers. Japanese port stocks were 238,000 t at end-May, the lowest since February 2012

Hormuz transits begin to normalise and release stranded Gulf metal - a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited the strait on 30-Jul, the FIRST in nearly three weeks, and oil eased as tankers continued to ply conflict-zone waters; the 15-Jun precedent was -4.4…

caveats: Report refreshed Thu 30-Jul-2026, ~06:20 London - BEFORE the LME ring. The benchmark table and lme_series carry the latest PUBLISHED LME aluminium official, which is the 29-Jul (Wednesday) settlement: cash $3,207.00 / 3M $3,177.00 / stock 267,800 t, from Westmetall. Today's official prints 13:20 London, so nothing here reflects today's session or today's Bank of England decision at 12:00 London. NOTE ON RETRIEVAL: Westmetall's default aluminium view initially returned data only through 28-Jul on the first request of this refresh; a cache-busted second request returned the 29-Jul row, which was then cross-checked against Reuters' 29-Jul intraday report ($3,176, +0.9%) and Trading Economics' 29-Jul close ($3,178.60, +0.95%).

THE BOARD IS ON A SINGLE UNIFORM SESSION THIS RUN. All five metals - aluminium, copper, nickel, zinc and lead - carry the 29-Jul official, and every day-change is 29-Jul versus 28-Jul. This is an improvement on the prior run, when nickel, zinc and lead lagged a session behind aluminium and copper because of Westmetall's progressive posting by metal.

THE HEADLINE SIGNAL IS A RELATIVE ONE AND SHOULD BE READ AS SUCH. Aluminium's 29-Jul rise is informative BECAUSE copper fell 0.4% on the same session with the dollar near one-month highs - it is a decoupling from the peer group, not a broad metals rally. That inference rests on Reuters' intraday reporting of copper and the dollar; the exchange officials confirm the aluminium leg but the attribution of cause (Gulf escalation) is Reuters' and is presented as such.

YTD percentages on the metals board are DERIVED, not exchange-published: each metal is measured against its own first-published 2026 LME 3-month official of 02-Jan-2026 (aluminium $3,010.50, copper $12,511.00, nickel $16,915.00, zinc $3,130.50, lead $2,008.00). Lead is the only board metal down year-to-date on that basis.

SPREAD CONVENTION AND THE SIGNAL: cash above 3M (positive cash-3M) is BACKWARDATION; cash below 3M is contango. On the 29-Jul official the spread NEARLY DOUBLED to +$30.00 while the flat price ROSE 1.07% - both in the same direction, the aligned tightening configuration. This follows 28-Jul, when the spread widened to +$16.00 against a 1.18% price FALL, which is the opposite-direction squeeze signature. The two-session sequence (+$11.00 to +$16.00 to +$30.00) through opposite flat-price moves is the more durable read; neither day alone would carry the same weight.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND SEVERAL ARE STALE. The freshest publicly retrievable prints in this report are 06-Jul-2026 (Platts: MJP/CIF Japan spot, Rotterdam duty-unpaid and duty-paid, US Midwest transaction) and 14-Jul-2026 (Fastmarkets: Rotterdam duty-paid). Each premium row is labelled with its own assessment date and is NOT marked to 30-Jul. A row that has not moved has not necessarily been unchanged - it has not been re-assessed in public. The tariff-versus-market decomposition IS refreshed every run because it is a function of the current LME cash.

ALUMINA AND RAW MATERIALS ARE ALSO PERIODIC AND OLDER STILL: SMM FOB Western Australia 09-Jul (21 days), CME Platts-linked futures 24-Jul (6 days), Platts FOB Australia 26-Jun, SMM Alumina Index 16-Jul, and Guinea bauxite CIF China early June because SMM's live assessments are paywalled. No alumina or bauxite figure in this report is a 30-Jul value.

THE EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID LINE CARRIES A CORRECTION MADE ON 29-JUL AND RETAINED HERE. Runs before that date carried $542.50/t on the EDU line; that figure is the midpoint of the Platts DUTY-PAID range ($525-560/t), while the correctly labelled duty-UNPAID assessment on the same 06-Jul date is $470-500/t, midpoint $485/t. Several secondary outlets reproduce the Platts story with the two mislabelled.

SECTION 232 DURATION - CORRECTION RETAINED. The 50%/25% aluminium rates originate in Proclamation 11021 of 02-Apr-2026 and carry NO stated end date. The 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window in the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (91 FR 34085) applies only to the Annex I-C REDUCED-RATE carve-outs. Separately, a proclamation of 20-Jul-2026 creates a Commerce-administered onshoring incentive allowing approved US-investment applicants to import at half the applicable rate; headline rates are unchanged and no CBP guidance for that measure had been issued at this refresh.

ROTTERDAM BILLET HAS NO JULY-2026 PUBLIC PRINT. The row carries Fastmarkets' 6063 extrusion billet ddp North Germany assessment of 29-May-2026 ($1,175-1,250/t, midpoint $1,212.50), explicitly described as 'the last available print' in trade coverage dated 20-Jul and now two months stale. Fastmarkets' calculated CIF Rotterdam billet premium is expected to first print 31-Jul.

THE HORMUZ PICTURE IS NOW TWO-WAY AND THE TWO DATA POINTS CONFLICT. On 29-Jul Tehran rejected Oman's transit proposal and airstrikes widened, driving crude up nearly 7%; on 30-Jul a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited the strait bound for Pakistan - the first in nearly three weeks - and oil slipped. Both are reported, both are sourced, and neither has been superseded. The report presents them side by side rather than resolving them.

ELLIOTT WAVE CONTENT IS TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE, and the daily confirmation this run rests on a MARGINAL break: the 29-Jul cash of $3,207.00 exceeded the 22-Jul wave (i) high of $3,205.00 by just $2.00. A single marginal close is weak confirmation and is flagged as such in the writeup, with explicit invalidation levels at $3,159.50 (re-opens wave (ii)) and $3,061.50 (voids the structure).

The forward projection band and sentiment history are GENERATED by the engine from price_history.json; they are not hand-authored. price_history.json samples the last official session of each week, and this run REPLACED the current week's row (previously 28-Jul) with the 29-Jul official rather than appending a duplicate.

PUBLIC INFORMATION ONLY. Every figure in this report traces to a public source with a URL. Nothing here is confidential, internal or company-specific, and nothing is framed as any particular company's position: there are no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary. The only company-specific content is public listed-company disclosure in the peer-earnings table.
